notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR18: for a GO TO transfer, "DEBUG-LINE identifies the GO TO statement whose execution transfers control to procedure-name-1" and DEBUG-NAME contains procedure-name-1. Each GO TO form sets __dbgCause = Transfer and __dbgLine to its own line before transferring (StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundGoTo), ControlFlowEmitter.EmitGoToDepending, AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitGoTo via EmitterState.EmitDebugCause); the subject's __RunDebug (DispatchEmitter.EmitDebugRunner) populates DEBUG-ITEM with that line, the subject's name and SPACES (DebugItem.Populate, ContentsFor). Probes at 85: GO TO PB OF S2 (line 21), GO TO ... DEPENDING ON (line 25), an ALTERed GO TO (line 29, the altered statement, not the GO TO that reached it), GO TO a section-name subject (line 33) and GO TO PB IN S2 (line 52) each report their own line and spaces; COBOL0902 at 2002/2023. The witness checks two GO TOs at one statement and a second statement.

next.reason: 1985: "DEBUG-LINE identifies the GO TO statement whose execution transfers control to procedure-name-1."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the debugging feature; USE and GO TO rules omit DEBUG-LINE, DEBUG-NAME and USE FOR DEBUGGING". No 2023 clause holds the Debug feature. The USE and GO TO candidates never mention USE FOR DEBUGGING, DEBUG-LINE or DEBUG-NAME, so the feature and this rule are dropped.
